note: Fixed examiner lines for IELTS mock tests. Each line is one recorded clip: public/audio/examiner/<id>.mp3. If a clip is missing, the browser voice reads the text. kind: say = examiner speaks and moves on; ask = the student answers (answerSeconds, or the Part 1 default when missing); wait = a short silent pause after the line (waitSeconds), with an optional on-screen hint (a key in messages practice.examiner).

lines.text: This is the Speaking test for the International English Language Testing System.
The candidate is Candidate 1, and the examiner is Augustus Flores.
Good morning.
Good afternoon.
Good evening.
My name is Augustus Flores.
Can you tell me your full name, please?
Thank you. And what shall I call you?
And can you tell me where you're from?
Can I see your identification, please?
Thank you, that's fine.
Now, in this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself.
Let's talk about where you live now.
Which town or city do you live in now?
Are there any things you don't like about your area? What are they?
Do you think you will continue to live there for a long time? Why, or why not?
Let's talk about what you do.
Do you work or are you a student?
What kind of work do you do?
What do you find most interesting about your work? Why?
Which is more important to you: the people you work with, or the work you do? Why?
What do you study?
What do you find most interesting about your studies? Why?
Which is more important to you: the teachers, or the other students on your course? Why?
Now, let's talk about a different topic.
lines.when: Part 1, before the mock's own topic

lines.text: Now, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes.
Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say.
You can make some notes if you wish.
Do you understand?
Here's some paper and a pencil for making notes, and here's your topic.
lines.when: Cue card appears after this line

lines.text: All right? Remember, you have one to two minutes for this, so don't worry if I stop you.
I'll tell you when the time is up. Can you start speaking now, please?
Thank you.
Can I have the booklet and the paper and pencil back, please?
Now, I'd like to discuss with you one or two more general questions related to this topic.
Thank you. That is the end of the speaking test.
